external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser outside the system's network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application that receives browser traffic and puts jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: A background worker process that picks up jobs and does the work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue receiving jobs from the web application for the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used to keep application log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The description does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: The config store from which the web application reads its settings and queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: The config store from which the worker reads its settings and database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: browser requests web application
data_flows.description: Traffic initiated by the browser to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: web application submits jobs to message queue
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: background worker picks up jobs from message queue
data_flows.description: The background worker picks up jobs from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the worker authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: background worker reads and writes database
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database, including application log records stored there.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the worker authenticates to the database.

data_flows.name: web application reads web application config
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings and credentials from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: background worker reads worker config
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings and credentials from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: and the worker has a worker config

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet outside the system's network.

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The web tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier containing the queue, worker, database and config stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because the browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that a user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The web application presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies it as a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker is a non-web process.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a background worker process that picks up queued jobs and does the work, rather than as an HTTP-family application interface.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config contains confidential data because it holds queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds the credentials the web application needs, including its queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config contains confidential data because it holds database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds the credentials the worker needs, including its database credentials.
